explanation: At its basic level, biodiversity represents the variety of species on Earth, with current estimates suggesting between 10 and 50 million species exist. An endangered species is defined as one in immediate danger of extinction throughout all or most of its range, whereas a threatened species is likely to become endangered in the near future. Ecologists describe biodiversity across three levels of biological organization: genetic diversity, community (ecosystem) diversity, and landscape diversity.

questions.q: What is the difference between an endangered species and a threatened species?
opts: Endangered species are plants, while threatened species are animals.
Endangered species are in immediate peril of extinction, while threatened species are likely to become endangered in the near future.
Endangered species have low genetic diversity, while threatened species are extinct.
There is no difference; they are defined identically by ecologists.

questions.q: What are the three levels of biological organization used to describe biodiversity?
opts: Genetic diversity, Community diversity, and Landscape diversity
